assumptions.service_distribution: independent lognormal calls, sigma=0.7; finite_pool_tradeoff uses explicit durations
assumptions.failures: seeded stage failures; successful siblings finish under both policies
assumptions.capacity: same finite shared pool and same per-stage ceilings in each comparison

interpretation: Ratios compare these sampled service times and capacities. A one-worker run has equal useful work; scheduling overhead can make chains slower. The unlimited-worker maximum-of-sums bound does not establish a finite-pool guarantee.
limits: No live models, token costs, network quotas, provider retry delays or semantic output quality are measured.

graph_scaling.workload: synthetic chain declared in reverse order
graph_scaling.scope: previous repeated readiness scan versus adjacency construction, topological validation and remaining-depth calculation; excludes method shape validation and execution
